about:
At 14, I tried to get into research labs in Bangladesh and was turned away. Not because of ability, but because of age. Research wasn't out of reach for students. It was gatekept.

I'm building **Project Q2** to make research a normal part of high school education, not a privilege for a few.

I wrote *A Child's Question to Kindness*, a short novel about a child who notices kindness slowly disappearing around him and starts asking why.

## Along the way

- International Children's Peace Prize, Top 30 Finalist
- IEEE conference presenter, NTU Singapore
- National Public Speaking Champion
- Johns Hopkins Global Health Leaders Conference Scholar
- Harvard Undergraduate Microbiology Society Junior Fellow

Written about in The Daily Star, Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune, Dhaka Post, Daily Sun and Bangladesh Pratidin.

quotes.text: The best books, he perceived, are those that tell you what you know already.
And, when you want something, all the universe conspires in helping you to achieve it.

We had given AM sentience. Inadvertently, of course, but sentience nonetheless. But it had been trapped. AM wasn't God, he was a machine. We had created him to think, but there was nothing it could do with that creativity.
